topic_summary: Analysis of daylight saving time (DST) as a biannual clock adjustment practice. The topic encompasses biological disruption from circadian misalignment, economic coordination benefits and costs, energy consumption claims, and the political economy of reform resistance despite widespread public opposition.

key_entities: Public opinion (majority opposition to clock changes)
key_tensions: Biological health costs vs economic coordination benefits
Public preference for abolition vs institutional inertia
Standard time vs permanent DST as abolition endpoint
key_mechanisms: Spring transition acute sleep deprivation (1-hour loss)
Chronic circadian misalignment under permanent DST (late sunrise)
Coordination lock-in via interstate commerce and broadcast schedules
Legislative capture by evening-daylight beneficiary industries
key_absences: Quantified health costs (cardiovascular events, accidents, productivity loss)
Distributional analysis (who bears biological costs vs who captures economic benefits)
International comparison (countries that abolished DST and outcomes)

axes.structural_delta: Measurable health and performance degradation from clock-biology desynchronization
axes.primary_observable: Sleep duration change, cardiovascular event rates, traffic accident rates in transition weeks; chronic late sleep phase under permanent DST
axes.selection_reason: Upstream mountain providing biological constraint base; distinct observable (circadian phase) independent of other axes

axes.structural_delta: Economic and operational costs of maintaining synchronized time zones across transportation, broadcast, and commerce systems
axes.primary_observable: Interstate commerce scheduling complexity, broadcast synchronization requirements, transportation timetable coordination costs
axes.selection_reason: Distinct observable (coordination costs) independent of biological axis; upstream to synthesis nodes

axes.human_readable: Coordination vs Health Tradeoff (DST as Imposed Compromise)
axes.structural_delta: DST practice as mechanism trading population health costs for coordination benefits and evening-daylight economic activity
axes.primary_observable: Retail/leisure revenue during extended evening daylight vs population health burden metrics
axes.selection_reason: Highest centrality; downstream synthesis of biological and coordination axes; distinct beneficiary/victim structure

axes.human_readable: Abolition Political Economy (Reform Resistance Despite Public Opposition)
axes.structural_delta: Legislative inertia and industry lobbying blocking DST abolition despite majority public support for ending clock changes
axes.primary_observable: Public opinion polling on DST abolition vs legislative action rates; industry lobbying expenditure
axes.selection_reason: Distinct political economy observable; captures reform blockage mechanism independent of underlying health/coordination tradeoff

axes.human_readable: Permanent DST vs Standard Time (Abolition Endpoint Dispute)
axes.structural_delta: Contested choice between permanent DST (late sunrise, chronic misalignment) vs permanent standard time (early sunset, coordination disruption)
axes.primary_observable: Winter sunrise times under each regime; public preference polling; chronobiologist consensus
axes.selection_reason: Distinct observable (abolition endpoint choice) independent of whether to abolish; captures intra-reform dispute

axes.structural_delta: Historical energy-saving rationale for DST no longer empirically supported but still cited in policy discourse
axes.primary_observable: Modern energy consumption studies vs policy justification rhetoric
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: captured as rhetorical component of abolition_political_economy snare; no independent structural delta beyond discourse analysis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Obsolete energy-saving rationale persisting in policy discourse
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Rhetorical component of abolition_political_economy; no independent structural delta beyond discourse analysis

omegas.description: Countries that abolished DST (Russia 2014, Turkey 2016) provide natural experiments. Outcomes unknown to model; could validate or invalidate coordination_infrastructure_lock_in severity.

Precise health burden quantification (DALYs, economic cost) absent from extraction. Mountain classification of circadian_misalignment_cost depends on magnitude; if costs are low, may reclassify to rope.

If permanent standard time is adopted, what is the actual coordination disruption cost? Rope classification of coordination_infrastructure_lock_in assumes non-trivial cost; empirical validation needed.
